_comment: Entries of the devices test engineer (PAIR UI, SRC, DEV sender, control room chat), same schema as tests/e2e/known-bugs.json; the orchestrator merges them. support/devices/bugs.ts (knownDevBug) reads this file until then. DEV-01 ... DEV-05 are open product bugs (their tests are expected failures); DEV-06 ... DEV-08 are documentation differences (the tests assert the product behaviour, the plan text is to be aligned).

DEV-01.title: A phone that comes back reports a false recovery for a few milliseconds: “K1 is back, was gone for N s”, then “K1 reconnecting” again with a new incident whose timer restarts at 00:00
DEV-01.steps: Phone K1 live in the program scene; cut its network (net.cut: setOffline + close WebSockets and peer connections); wait 3-20 s; restore. Read the studio hub events and the production log.
DEV-01.expected: One “K1 reconnecting” at the start of the outage, one “K1 is back, was gone for N s” when the picture is really back; N is the length of the outage; the incident timer keeps counting in between.
DEV-01.actual: 30-40 ms after the network is back (hub reconnected, the track is still published at LiveKit, the old session state says live) the API emits sourceUpserted K1 ok + incidentUpserted(endedAt) + log “K1 is back, was gone for N s”; 7-10 ms later the first report of the reconnected sender says rtc: reconnecting: sourceUpserted K1 reconnecting + incidentRemoved + a NEW incidentUpserted + log “K1 reconnecting”. The real recovery follows 7-9 s later with “K1 is back, was gone for 8 s” (the first 4-20 s of the outage are not counted). Log shows two “reconnecting” and two “is back” entries for one outage; the strip timer jumps back to 00:00. Reproduced 5 times (outage 3, 4, 5, 9, 20 s).
DEV-01.evidence: The test attaches hub-events.txt (log entries and K1 source events); studio hub timeline of the five runs (relative to net.restore): +32 ms sourceUpserted K1 ok, incidentUpserted(endedAt), log “K1 is back, was gone for 9 s”; +41 ms sourceUpserted K1 reconnecting, incidentRemoved, incidentUpserted(open), log “K1 reconnecting”; +8531 ms sourceUpserted K1 ok, log “K1 is back, was gone for 8 s”.
DEV-01.fix: A hub reconnect (Hello of the same session) must not turn a slot `ok` before the session has reported again: keep rtc/slot state `reconnecting` until the first report after the reconnect, or do not count a published track as live while the last known device rtc state was reconnecting/disconnected.

DEV-02.title: After a short phone outage the picture is back 7-9 s after the network returns (T-RECOVER-SHORT hard limit 3 s): the SDK reconnect backoff is not reset when the network is back
DEV-02.steps: Phone K1 live; net.cut(phone context); wait 3 / 5 / 9 / 20 s; net.restore; poll the Regie (station row, strip) every 100 ms.
DEV-02.expected: T-RECOVER-SHORT: outage <= 10 s: network back -> picture and “back” within 3 s (target 2 s).
DEV-02.actual: 7.1 s (5 s outage), 7.4 s (20 s), 7.8 s (4 s), 8.5 s (9 s), 8.9 s (3 s) until `ok`. Phone console: LiveKit `detected network reconnected` at +11 ms, `resuming signal connection, attempt 4` at +1138 ms, signal connected at +1146 ms, `reconnect disconnected` at +1147 ms (the resume cannot succeed: the peer connection was closed), then `reconnecting, attempt: 5` only at +5968 ms (EndlessReconnectPolicy: backoffDelay(5) = 4800 ms + jitter), connected at +7992 ms. E2E_BUG_REPORT=1 runs of the test: frames advancing again 6405 / 6506 / 7562 ms after the network is back, “back” 8379 ms (outage 9 s).
DEV-02.evidence: The test attaches recover-short.json; E2E_BUG_REPORT=1 run: frames advancing 6405 ms and “back” 8379 ms after the network is back (outage 9 s). Phone console timeline (+ms after net.restore): detected network reconnected +11, resuming signal connection attempt 4 +1138, signal connected +1146, reconnect disconnected +1147, reconnecting attempt 5 +5968, connection state reconnecting -> connected +7992.
DEV-02.fix: Reset the SDK reconnect attempt (and with it the escalated delay) when the page reports `online` / wakes, e.g. restart the media session on the wake signal while it is `reconnecting`, not only while it is `waiting`; or cap the SDK policy lower while the network is known to be back.

DEV-03.title: A phone tab that was replaced by another tab (“Opened in another tab”) keeps its screen wake lock
DEV-03.steps: Phone live in tab 1 (wake lock held); open the sender in tab 2 of the same browser; tab 1 shows “Opened in another tab”; read navigator.wakeLock (stub counting request/release).
DEV-03.expected: docs/testing.md E2E-SRC-11: tab 1 releases camera and wake lock; the live tab holds it; after “Continue here” the roles swap.
DEV-03.actual: Tab 1 released the camera (slot paused) but its wake lock stays active (request count 1, released 0) for as long as the tab is replaced: DeviceSessionService.updateDerived() only treats removed/stopped as terminal; the camera slot is `paused` after the release, which counts as sending, so wakeLock.enable() runs again. Reproduced twice.
DEV-03.evidence: E2E_BUG_REPORT=1 run (twice): “tab 1 released the wake lock” expected 0, received 1 after 5 s (test E2E-SRC-11 [ui, wake lock]); the wake lock stub counts request/release.
DEV-03.fix: In updateDerived() treat phase `replaced` (and `blocked`) like a terminal phase for the wake lock: disable it while the session is not the active one.

DEV-04.title: At 1280 x 720 the tab row of the pairing dock (Phone / Laptop / Link) collapses to 2 px height while the Phone tab shows its QR code; the tab buttons are covered by the panel and cannot be clicked
DEV-04.steps: Regie at 1280 x 720 (the default viewport of the harness), click “Pair device” (the dock opens on the tab “Laptop”), click the tab “Phone” (works: the Laptop panel is short), wait for the QR code, then try to click the tab “Laptop” or “Link” again.
DEV-04.expected: The tabs are visible and clickable (a tab button is 32 px high); DEV-01: critical controls reachable at 1280 x 720.
DEV-04.actual:
getBoundingClientRect: .c-tabs 320 x 2 px at (307,465), tab buttons 106 x 32 px overflowing it, the panel (.c-pair__panel, 282 px) starts at y=475 and covers them; Playwright: the click on the tab is intercepted by the panel text (

) or the dock header, 15 s timeout. On the Laptop and Link tabs the row is 34 px high (the panels are shorter). Only the keyboard (focus + Enter) switches tabs from the Handy tab. Reproduced in every run that clicked a tab after the QR code had loaded.
DEV-04.evidence: E2E_BUG_REPORT=1 run (twice): tab row height 2, expected >= 30 (test E2E-PAIR-01 [ui, dock tabs]); screenshot tests/e2e/.output/sf-e2e-2/artifacts/devices-pair-ui-PAIR-phone-74a92--Regie-the-code-is-replaced-smoke/test-failed-1.png of an earlier run shows the hairline above the QR code; measured: .c-tabs 307,465 320x2, tab button 308,466 106x32, panel 307,475 320x282.
DEV-04.fix: Give the tab row flex: none (or min-height) so the panel scrolls instead of the tabs shrinking; or scroll the dock body, not the tab row.

DEV-05.title: Sender dark mode: the slot code (“K1”) and the hint “Tap for controls” are dim grey on black, below the WCAG AA contrast (2.96:1 and 2.35:1)
DEV-05.steps: Pair a phone, start the camera, press “Dark”; run axe (wcag2a, wcag2aa) on the black screen.
DEV-05.expected: docs/testing.md E2E-DEV-15: 0 critical/serious axe violations (colour-contrast findings reviewed individually).
DEV-05.actual: axe color-contrast (serious): .c-phone__dark-code #53595f on #000000 = 2.96:1 (needs 3:1 for large text); .c-phone__dark-hint #464a4f on #000000 = 2.35:1 (needs 4.5:1). Every other state of the phone and laptop sender passes axe (wcag2a, wcag2aa) without findings. The dimness is probably intended (no glare on a stage); it needs either a decision (accepted finding with reason) or a lighter grey.
DEV-05.fix: Lighten the text colours of .c-phone__dark-code (to about #767c84 or lighter, 4.5:1 on black) and .c-phone__dark-hint, or accept the colour-contrast rule for the dark screen with a written reason.

DEV-06.title: docs/testing.md E2E-SRC-01 pins the health chip “All N stations ok” (regex ^All d+ stations ok$); the product writes “1 station ok” for exactly one station (selectors.ts stationsOkText) and “No stations” for none
DEV-06.resolution: The tests of this folder accept “All N stations ok” and “1 station ok”. The plan text (E2E-SRC-01, E2E-SRC-03, E2E-PAIR-17) should say “1 station ok” for one station.
DEV-06.expected: docs/testing.md E2E-SRC-01 / -03: “1 station ok” for one station.

DEV-07.title: Several UI texts and measures of docs/testing.md differ from the product (all intended, the tests assert the product): link box shows “host/j/{token}” without https:// (the clipboard holds the full https URL); after “Stop sharing” the sender offers “Share again” (not “Share screen”); the pending-cap notice is “Too many attempts. Please try again in N seconds.” (plan: /later/); the check code on the sender is at least 24 px mono (clamp 36-56 px, plan: 24 px); the title “Phone as a camera” of the pairing dock is hidden on short laptops (height <= 820 px, by design); the platform text of Chrome on Android is “Android · Chrome” (Chrome reduces the user agent, no model); Chrome on an iPad profile keeps getDisplayMedia, so it is a laptop unless the API is absent as in Safari
DEV-07.resolution: Tests assert the product texts and measures; GAP-27 style regexes of the plan should be replaced by the exact strings.
DEV-07.expected: docs/testing.md E2E-PAIR-10 (URL box), E2E-SRC-08, E2E-PAIR-16, E2E-DEV-10, E2E-PAIR-01, E2E-PAIR-15 to follow the product.

DEV-08.title: docs/testing.md E2E-DEV-11 asks for 8 px between adjacent tap targets and E2E-DEV-17 lists “Station(s)” as a word of the other language: the options of a segmented control (Front/Back, 720p/1080p, Phone/Laptop) are joined by design (0 px apart, each option is 44 px or more high and wide), and “Station” is a German word as well (“Station starting”, “This station is now running in another tab or window”)
DEV-08.resolution: E2E-DEV-11 checks the 8 px gap between separate controls only (options of one fieldset are excluded); E2E-DEV-17 leaves “Station” out of the English word list.
DEV-08.expected: docs/testing.md E2E-DEV-11 and E2E-DEV-17 to name the exceptions.
